Toronto Stock Exchange Soars to Another Record High with Interest-Sensitive Issues and Conglomerates Driving the Market

The Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX) hit a new record high yesterday, following a surge in interest-sensitive issues, such as banks and insurers, and conglomerates. The TSX increased by 0.56% to 20,142.78, representing its third consecutive day of gains.

This impressive leap in the market was primarily driven by the Bank of Canada's decision to hold its interest rate steady at 0.25%, which supports banks and life insurers. According to analysts, this move has boosted the economic outlook, which has been struggling due to the pandemic's impact.

The market's conglomerates also played a significant role. Brookfield Asset Management Inc., one of the biggest names in the TSX, experienced a 3.2% increase in its shares, representing its highest increase in almost a year. This leap was primarily due to the successful sale of Oaktree Capital Group, LLC's stake in a fund managed by the global alternative asset manager.

The Building Societies Association (BSA) is considering taking the issue of draft legislation on takeover protection to a European Court of Justice. BSA believes the legislation poses the risk of putting thousands of small British firms and their shareholders, into great financial distress. The proposed legislation, introduced by a coalition government under the Financial Services Bill, enables UK companies to delay the payment of taxes if they have to pay large sums of money to acquire a controlling stake in a business.

The BSA has warned that the legislation could result in thousands of companies having to hand over substantial amounts of cash to acquire a controlling stake in their businesses, leading to difficult financial circumstances and even insolvency. The BSA has suggested that the legislation breaches European Union (EU) merger regulations, creating major legal uncertainties and increasing political risk for the UK.

Additionally, the BSA argues that the UK could fall foul of legal regulations, including those governing cross-border acquisitions, if the legislation is allowed to stand.

When Joseph and Mary decided it was time to tell their son Jesus about where babies come from, Joseph and Mary told the story.
“Listen to me, Jesus. There is no such thing as magic. No fairy dust that can bring you to a different time and place.”
The little Jesus rolled his eyes. “Grandma?” he asked.
“No, son. Grandma had the same fairy dust idea when she was your age.”
The little Jesus tilted his head. “Did she?”
“Yes, but she thought it was because she had been blessed by a fairy,” Mary chuckled. “It was because you were smart and your grandmother loved you. And you were the same age as Jesus now and had the same idea that made her want to bring you in time and space.”
“So it was my imagination,” said the little Jesus. “I am the same age as Jesus.

“Listen to me, Jesus. There is no such thing as magic. No fairy dust that can bring you to a different time and place.”
The little Jesus rolled his eyes. “Grandma?” he asked.
“No, son. Grandma had the same fairy dust idea when she was your age.”
The little Jesus tilted his head. “Did she?”
“Yes, but she thought it was because she had been blessed by a fairy,” Mary chuckled. “It was because you were smart and your grandmother loved you. And you were the same age as Jesus now and had the same idea that made her want to bring you in time and space.”
“So it was my imagination,” said the little Jesus. “I am the same age as Jesus.

The sun was setting in the distance, casting an orange glow across the battlefield. The sound of clashing swords filled the air as the armies clashed amidst the chaos. Soldiers were falling left and right, unable to withstand the power of the ancient weapons wielded by their adversaries. At that exact moment, a young soldier charged forth towards the enemy.

The soldier had a spear, and as he drew it back to strike, something caught his eye. The weapon had been battered and worn, but as he gazed into the shadows beneath the warrior's skin, he could see that there was a glimmer of something hidden behind his cheek and nose.

Curiosity getting the better of him, the young soldier leaned in slightly, ready to strike down his first foe, when his eyes fell upon the shimmering weapon. In that moment of hesitation, the soldier decided to do something brave and foolish.

I was feckin' sloshed, mate. First time I ever was in the Big Lemon, and I'd found me the best feckin' pub I could imagine, I tell ya what. So I stumble out when it was closin' time, musta been'round 4 o'clock in the morning, and made my way through some alleys to find the quaint little AirBnB place I'd rented for the week.  

The cobblestone streets were like an obstacle course to my blurred vision and unsteady feet. I lurched left, then right, grasping at the old brick walls to keep from toppling over. The pale yellow light of the streetlamps glowed fuzzy and indistinct. I blinked hard, trying to bring the world into some semblance of focus and figure out which twisting alley I had wandered into.  

Nothing looked familiar. Panic started to rise in my throat, choking out the laughter that had filled me just moments before.

I never liked my mother’s cookies. They were too sweet for my taste and they never seemed to come out of the oven just right. But the rest of the town disagreed with me, for every year my mother, or as the town called her, the “Cookie Lady,” would bake hundreds of batches of cookies during the holiday season. Her cookies were the talk of the town, with people coming from miles away just to get a taste.

I remember asking her once what her secret ingredient was, but she only gave me a sly smile and said, “It’s a secret.” I never pried too much, but as I got older, I realized that my mother was becoming more and more protective of the recipe. She would guard it like it was a precious gem, making sure to never let it slip out of her grasp.

Thanks for reading my story!
He’d be thirty-three years old this July. If you could see him now, he’d be laughing.
He’d have a career. A family. A house.
He’d have a girlfriend. Or maybe a wife.
He’d be proud. Happy. Loving.
He would be happy.
Because he had seen the future.
It looked good, he said. Better than good. The best.
He had a plan. He had things he was going to do, places he was going to go.
But the future would never come for him.
He was an angel now. An angel without wings.
He had told the story. And then he’d gone.
She would be twenty-three next month, and while she had a career, a family, and a house, a girlfriend and a potential wife, she was not happy.
He had died when she was six.
A young girl.

Maria had always been the favorite child of her parents. She was smart, beautiful and obedient. Her younger sister, Sofia, was nothing like her. She was rebellious, mischievous, and always caused trouble. At least, that's how their parents saw her.

One day, when Sofia accidentally broke a vase, she knew she was in trouble. Maria saw an opportunity to win more favor with their parents and came up with a plan. She would tell their parents that she had broken the vase and that Sofia had tried to cover it up.

It worked. Her parents praised her honesty and punished Sofia for lying. But the guilt ate away at Maria. She knew that she had done something deceitful. Her relationship with her sister was never the same again.

Years later, as adults, Maria could no longer carry the weight of the lie. She approached Sofia and confessed everything.

The humans had always believed that the universe was vast and mysterious, with no end in sight. But now, after years of searching, they had finally discovered the truth. The universe, as we know it, was just an alien kid's experiment for his science fair.

The humans had spent years studying the stars and galaxies, trying to figure out what they were and how they worked. But no matter how hard they tried, they could not understand the mysteries of the universe.

Until one day, when an alien kid had come to Earth and told the humans that the universe was just an experiment he had been conducting for his science fair. The humans were amazed and curious, and they decided to investigate further.

They spent years studying the alien kid's experiment, and finally, they had succeeded in understanding the mysteries of the universe.

Suddenly, a loud noise interrupted the peaceful atmosphere. The sound was like a stampede of horses galloping out of control, accompanied by the unmistakable rattle of metal.

As people rushed around trying to find the source of the noise, a middle-aged man suddenly came barrelling down the sidewalk, a look of intense rage upon his face. He shouted a string of words in a foreign language, his face turning red with anger. His arms were flailing wildly as he careened towards a nearby building, narrowly missing a group of pedestrians.

I took a deep breath and steeled myself for what was to come. As Sergeant of the Alpha Squad, I had just given the order to pull back from defending the bridge. It was an impossible fight, and staying would mean certain death for all my soldiers. 

But as I turned around, I was faced with five rifle barrels pointed at my face. My own squad, my loyal soldiers who I had led through hell and back, were now turning their weapons on me.

“Stand down!” I bellowed. But they did not waver.

“We don't abandon our posts!” yelled Jax, always the most bullheaded of the group. I saw the anger and betrayal in his eyes.

“Stand down, that's an order!” I repeated. But it was clear words were not going to solve this problem. I had two choices. Follow my order and pull back, avoiding a slaughter but destroying the trust of my squad.

When she lost her job, she didn't know what to do. It was the only thing that gave her a sense of purpose and an income. She sank into a dark place, where she didn't want to talk to anyone or leave her apartment. Her friends tried to cheer her up, but their words were empty. They didn't understand how she felt, how lost and hopeless she was.

That's when he came into her life. They had met before, but they were never close. He noticed that something was wrong and asked her what was going on. She opened up to him, telling him about her struggles and how she felt like a failure. He listened to her without judgment, without trying to tell her what to do or how to feel.

One day, he came over to her apartment, bringing with him pizza, beer, and a movie.

The Letter 

I stared at the crumpled piece of paper in my hands, reading and rereading the contents. My brow furrowed as I tried to make sense of what I was seeing.

It was a letter, apparently from myself, dated exactly one year in the future. But that was impossible. How could I be receiving a letter from myself in the future? 

I read through the short missive again:

Dear [My Name], 

I know this will sound strange, but I am writing to you from one year in the future. I have some instructions for you—some very specific things you need to do today in order to ensure certain events unfold as they should. I can't explain why, but trust that following these instructions is of the utmost importance. 

Here is what you must do today:

1. Visit the corner coffee shop at 9:32 am. Order a double espresso and a blueberry muffin.

Once upon a time, in the peaceful city of Harmonyville, lived a retired super villain named Draven. After years of causing mayhem and devastation, Draven had turned over a new leaf, leaving his villainous life behind. Now, he spent his days taking care of his adorable 6-year-old daughter, Lily, who was the light of his life.

modified: Dreams are funny things. You may think you are just going to sleep, but before you know it you are running through a jungle, struggling to breathe while a panting gorilla looks on. Once upon a time, in a world not so different from our own, a unique tradition shaped the lives of many. At the tender age of 10, each child was gifted a companion animal, a loyal friend that would grow and evolve alongside them, influencing their paths and molding their character. The animals assigned to each child were based on their behavior during childhood, revealing the true essence of their personalities.
In the quaint village of Oakbrook, young Alice eagerly anticipated her 10th birthday when she would finally be united with her companion animal. She had spent her childhood days exploring the forests, tending to sick animals, and showing endless compassion for all living creatures. Rumors spread in hushed whispers that Alice would receive a majestic and rare companion animal.
When the special day finally arrived, the village square bustled with excitement. Families stood together, as parents proudly watched their children receive their companion animals.

As I sat in my kitchen, savoring my morning meal, a man in a lab coat appeared at the door. I assumed it was just another stranger, so I returned the smile and said goodbye, but he just stared at me with those eyes I couldn't quite place, like he was trying to look straight into my soul.

"Thank you for your time," he quietly said, without any real explanation.

"Oh, don't mention it," I replied, wondering what could have been in the experiment he wanted to end.

But instead of leaving, he walked around the kitchen, peering into the cabinets and the pantry. I didn't think much of it, only noticed the odd way he moved, as if he was searching for something.

"Do you know what I'm doing?" he asked, a sudden glint in his eyes.

"Well, I don't know but it sounds interesting." I replied, trying to keep my tone casual.

In this world, the practice of cloud harvesting, or retrieving the water droplets from the clouds, was a dangerous and perilous job. In an alternate universe, marriage was unlike anything known on the Earth. It was a bond that went beyond a lifetime commitment. The binding was so strong that when either one of the partners died, their counterpart would also drop dead almost instantly. The ceremony involved a ritual drink that bonded them for eternity, and no one knew if it was a curse or a blessing.

Zoe and Tom were in love since their teenage years and wanted to be together forever. As natural as it seemed, it was a difficult decision for them to pledge their life to each other. After all, they were young, and they had their whole life ahead of them, and making a commitment like this was daunting. But, as few did, they took the plunge. 

Years went by, and their love blossomed, until one day Tom fell ill. The doctors tried everything, but it was too late.

I just discovered that my future self has visited the past.
As I entered the past, I was transported back to the time I was born, and met my future self.
I was stunned to see myself. She looks exactly like I do now, but is dressed in a white night dress, and is pregnant.
She is sitting in an old wooden chair, holding a blue box that she is holding, and as I get closer she gives it to me.
"Here you go, it's a phone box." She says. "In my time, when you need to call someone you just look at the phone and talk to them. So you use it to call yourself."
My mind started whirling, could this be possible? But she seemed so real.
"You look so familiar," she says, "I met you in my future, but we never spoke, we just nodded at each other.

The old warehouse was in flames, the fire raging as the fire trucks arrived. But this was no accident. I started that fire, to destroy the evidence of what really happened. To cover my tracks, eliminate any trace of my presence here tonight. As the flames erupted around me, I slipped out the back into the darkness, rushing home as sirens echoed in the distance.

24 hours earlier

"You need to do this, Tom. We're counting on you." The voices on the phone were insistent. I didn't want this burden, this responsibility that could change everything. But I owed them. After years of working together, of having each other's backs, I couldn't say no.  

That's how I found myself staking out the warehouse that night, waiting for the familiar blue van to appear. The one that made deliveries once a month, always late at night when the streets were deserted.

They were sitting in a tiny room, looking at themselves in the mirror. They were the same person; but their appearance had changed.
The old ones, who had seen such changes before, had not expected this one to happen. The old ones had even created a whole new race to keep the death-less creatures happy. The old ones had worked so hard at it, that the war to eradicate death had been a success.
"What do we do now?" the old ones asked. "Shouldn't we start creating some new life forms to keep our creatures busy? I have the new race, but they are just useless. They are like the plants in our garden. They need water. Water that's not found here. And the new plants are only going to grow here. And they'll just stay here."
"Do you think they can live forever without new life?"
"Yes.

The old logging trail was overgrown but still visible to John as he made his way through the dense forest. His backpack was heavy with supplies for his final days. After 60 years of struggling with depression, he was ready to end it. 

As he reached a small clearing, he was surprised to see another man sitting on a large rock, staring intently at a bottle of pills in his hands. John coughed to announce his presence. The man looked up, startled.

They stared at each other for a moment, an unspoken understanding passing between them. "I guess we had the same idea," the man said grimly.

John nodded. "I'm John."

"Mark," the other man replied.  

An awkward silence fell. John didn't know what to say. He had planned to find solitude, not company. But something about knowing this stranger, Mark, made his own decision feel suddenly less sure.

Mark broke the silence.

The morning fog slowly rolled in, obscuring the horizon and casting a soft gray glow over the small village of Shiverton. The sounds of children playing and birds chirping filled the air as the dewy grass glistened in the rising sunlight. It was a peaceful scene, but it would have been an altogether different sight had one not glanced up. The sky to the east had just begun to brighten from a beautiful cerulean blue to a roaring, glorious red. From this village, many miles away, a beautiful maiden watched in silent awe. 

She had just emerged from the forest onto the ancient burial mound that served as her home. She glanced over to her right, where several of her friends were already beginning their daily patrol. It had been weeks since the mysterious Shield Maiden had appeared in their sleepy little village, and everyone was eager to learn her secret.

The sky to the east had just begun to brighten from a beautiful cerulean blue to a roaring, glorious red. From this village, many miles away, a beautiful maiden watched in silent awe. 

She had just emerged from the forest onto the ancient burial mound that served as her home. She glanced over to her right, where several of her friends were already beginning their daily patrol. It had been weeks since the mysterious Shield Maiden had appeared in their sleepy little village, and everyone was eager to learn her secret.

I thought I was the villain in this tale. I had it all planned out. The traps were set, the evil plot devised, the heroes walking right into my clutches.

Then he did the unthinkable. He didn't fall for any of my tricks or schemes. He evaded every snare.  But he didn't gloat or retaliate. He just gave me that infuriating smile of his, as if he knew something I didn't. 

When I finally had him cornered, monologuing like a fool, he put his hand on my shoulder and said "It doesn't have to be this way." His eyes were unbearably kind.

In that moment, something inside me cracked. The anger and hatred drained away, leaving me hollow. I suddenly saw with awful clarity the depths I had sunk to, the hurt I had caused.

I stumbled back, everything I thought I knew in tatters around me. "What have I done?" I choked out.

Once upon a time, in a small village nestled among rolling green hills, there lived a group of dreamers. They were ordinary people with extraordinary dreams that reached far beyond the confines of their everyday lives. These dreamers believed in the power of imagination and the endless possibilities that lay within their minds.
Among the dreamers was a young girl named Lily. Since she was a child, Lily had dreamed of flying high above the clouds, feeling the wind rush through her hair. She would often spend hours lying in open fields, staring up at the vast expanse of the sky, her eyes filled with wonder and longing. Lily's parents would often laugh and say, "Silly Lily, you're just a dreamer!" However, deep within her heart, Lily believed that her dreams held a truth she had yet to discover.
One day, news spread throughout the village that a fair was coming to town.

I never understood why people insist on getting wasted every night. All the liquid courage in the world can’t change the fact that you are a broken human being the following morning. I, however, am not perfect, and I fully admit that I was a poor judge of character the previous evening. 

I was too distracted by all of the fascinating stories swapping tales of adventure around the large wooden table, when out of the blue a tall, burly man at the end of the bar suddenly started telling us an epic tale of derring-do. With each boastful word, I found myself growing more intrigued. I felt like I was in the middle of a story, and I was the only one holding back laughter at the man’s childlike exaggeration. The more he spoke, the harder I smiled, and soon I was engaged in the tale.

As he drew closer and closer, the tension in the air grew stronger and stronger. No one knew who this stranger was, or why he was here, but everyone could feel it.

modified:
Every day, like clockwork, my normal day consists of 25 hours instead of 24. It's something I have grown accustomed to, as though I am given an extra slice of time to spend just the way I please. Once a day, for an hour, the world stops except for me.
In this enchanted hour, I am free to explore the stillness that surrounds me. The silence is profound and soothing, as if the universe wants to give me undivided attention. Every day, I use this extraordinary hour to immerse myself in the beauty of the world that temporarily rests.
As soon as the clock strikes the designated moment, everything freezes in place. People halt mid-step, birds suspended in the air, and leaves hold their breath on the branches. It is a bizarre sight, but one that I have embraced with wonder. What used to be a fearful experience has now turned into a cherished routine.

I woke up with a start, my heart thrumming with a sense of urgency. I knew who I was in my past life - I had been murdered. I remembered the pain, the fear. But now I also remembered the face of the person who had killed me.

I spent weeks tracking down my killer. I accessed memories of my past life with a new level of clarity, using every detail available to me to piece together the clues. I did things I'd never thought possible, leveraging my past experiences and my newfound determination to bring justice to the person who had taken my life.

Finally, I found him. He was living under a different name, but I recognized him instantly. He was older now, with more wrinkles and less hair, but he still had the same cold, dead eyes.

I followed him for days, watching him go about his mundane routine.

I woke up to the sound of my phone buzzing on the wooden bedside table of the hotel room. Rubbing my eyes, I reached for the device and saw a notification for a work email. Unwilling to dwell on it, I got up and headed out to explore the city.

As I walked around, admiring the architecture and the hustle and bustle of the busy streets, I couldn't help but feel inspired. I started typing on my phone, weaving my experiences and surroundings into a story.

At a café, I took a break and looked up from my phone screen. The aroma of fresh coffee filled the air as baristas expertly brewed different blends. I added the café setting to my story, describing the espresso machine's steam and the sound of beans being ground.

Feeling adventurous, I headed towards the river and walked across a bridge. Below, boats floated lazily downstream.

"I remember the first day of ninth grade when the bell rang and the crowd rushed in like a hurricane. I stood there frozen and lost in thought, unsure of what to do next. I watched as everyone came to class and I saw a couple students approach me. I watched as they spoke to me, saying my name over and over again. Introduction

Sexual orientation has long been a topic of controversy and discussion in society. The ongoing debate over whether individuals are born gay or become gay due to environmental factors has been raging for years. However, recent research seems to suggest that the environment plays a more significant role in shaping people's sexual orientation than previously thought. This essay will explore the impact of the environment on people's sexual orientation by examining the relationship between the respondents' assigned sex at birth and their sexual orientation. We will consider the differing environments surrounding males and females, and investigate how these differences may influence individuals' identification with their sexual orientation.

Introduction

This essay will explore the impact of the environment on people's sexual orientation by examining the relationship between the respondents' assigned sex at birth and their sexual orientation. We will consider the differing environments surrounding males and females, and investigate how these differences may influence individuals' identification with their sexual orientation.

Defining Sexual Orientation

Sexual orientation refers to an individual's attraction to a particular sex or gender. An individual can be attracted to people of the same sex (homosexual), opposite sex (heterosexual), or both sexes (bisexual).

The French historian Fernand Braudel made a significant contribution to the Annales school of history and challenged traditional historical methods with his emphasis on the longue durée. Braudel advocated studying history at multiple timescales, including the short-term events studied in traditional political and social history, but also longer-term geographical, social, and economic factors that shape historical change. 

Braudel articulated his vision for a new historical method in his 1949 book La Méditerranée et le Monde Méditerranéen à l'époque de Philippe II. In this work, Braudel examined the Mediterranean world in the 16th century, but rather than focusing on the political and military events surrounding the reign of Philip II of Spain, Braudel spent much of the book discussing the geography of the Mediterranean and long-term social and economic factors like trade, agriculture, and transportation. For Braudel, these were the deep historical forces that shaped human events and experiences in the Mediterranean over the long run.

Tsunamis are massive ocean waves that are caused by abrupt displacements of large volumes of water. They are usually generated by earthquakes occurring below or near the ocean floor, but can also be caused by underwater landslides or volcanic eruptions. Unlike typical surface waves on the ocean that are generated by wind, tsunamis travel at very high speeds across the open ocean, up to 500 miles per hour. As the tsunami approaches the shore, the shallowing sea floor causes the tsunami to slow down, decrease in wavelength, and increase dramatically in height. Tsunamis can reach up to 100 feet high at the coast, causing catastrophic damage.

The key difference between tsunamis and regular wind-generated waves is their source of energy. Wind creates waves by transferring its kinetic energy to the water's surface. The energy and power of wind waves depends on factors like wind speed, duration of wind, and the distance over which the wind is blowing.

original:
Infertility is the inability to become pregnant after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse. While a few causes are purely genetic, a vast majority of causes are environmental. While there has been an overall decrease in the rate of infertility across the developed world, the rate of male infertility has remained relatively constant. This is in part due to a lack of male factor testing and in part to cultural and systemic sexism that relegates the concerns of men to the medical sphere while women are expected to adopt a more heroic, "just try harder" attitude toward pregnancy.

Given the current rates of infertility in the United States, it's important to examine the potential psychological effects on those who face the challenge of infertility. While there are multiple types of infertility, primary infertility is caused by problems with the man and/or the woman's reproductive organs.

original:
Henrik Ibsen's 1879 play'A Doll's House' exemplifies many of the characteristics of the naturalist drama movement of the late 19th century. Naturalism in drama aimed to represent'real life' on stage as truthfully and objectively as possible. Ibsen adopted this approach in'A Doll's House' through focusing on the lives of middle-class people and their daily struggles and relationships. The play has a strong focus on the psychology and inner experiences of the characters in place of melodramatic plotlines and action. The characters are ordinary people grappling with family dynamics, relationships, gender roles and self-identity. This focus on internal, psychological elements was a hallmark of naturalism in drama. 

Ibsen also employed highly detailed, elaborate stage directions in the text of'A Doll's House' in order to prescribe the most realistic and lifelike staging of the play. The stage directions span several pages at the beginning of the play, describing in extensive detail the set, furnishings, lighting and daily activities of the characters.

Hyperlipidemia refers to abnormally high levels of lipids, such as cholesterol and triglycerides, in the blood. Elevated lipid levels are a risk factor for coronary heart disease, including heart attacks and coronary artery disease. There are several classes of pharmaceutical treatments available for hyperlipidemia to help lower lipid levels and reduce coronary heart disease risk.

Statins are the most commonly prescribed class of drugs for lowering cholesterol. Statins work by inhibiting the enzyme HMG-CoA reductase, which plays a key role in cholesterol production. By blocking this enzyme, statins reduce the amount of cholesterol made by the liver. Statins have been shown in numerous large clinical trials to effectively lower LDL or "bad" cholesterol and reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes. Some of the most widely used statins include atorvastatin (Lipitor), simvastatin (Zocor), rosuvastatin (Crestor), and pravastatin (Pravachol). Lowering LDL cholesterol by just 1% can reduce the risk of coronary heart disease by 1 to 2%.

As e-commerce continues to grow, governments around the world are struggling to keep up with the new digital landscape. The lack of uniform regulations creates a complex web of rules and legal requirements that businesses must navigate to comply with national and international laws.

One example of this is the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which took effect in 2018. Western Australia’s largest global partnerships in its liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry —Woodside Petroleum and industry giants BHP, Chevron, Shell, and Mitsubishi—announced a plan to double production in the North West Shelf (NWS) project today. The partners have proposed a A$6 billion joint investment to ensure the NWS will continue to operate for decades to come. 

The NWS is one of Australia's crucial LNG production complexes, responsible for about 42% of the country's LNG production. The project, based in Western Australia's Pilbara region, includes five offshore gas and condensate fields and an onshore LNG processing facility near Karratha.
original:
Western Australia’s largest global partnerships in its liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry —Woodside Petroleum and industry giants BHP, Chevron, Shell, and Mitsubishi—announced a plan to double production in the North West Shelf (NWS) project today. The partners have proposed a A$6 billion joint investment to ensure the NWS will continue to operate for decades to come. 

The NWS is one of Australia's crucial LNG production complexes, responsible for about 42% of the country's LNG production. The project, based in Western Australia's Pilbara region, includes five offshore gas and condensate fields and an onshore LNG processing facility near Karratha.

Under the proposed expansion, the project would produce another 6 million tonnes per year. Once completed, the NWS expansion would represent a significant boost to Australia’s natural gas sector, creating jobs and strengthening the economy.

The partners expect to complete the final investment decision (FID) process for the expansion project in the second half of 2021 and begin operations in 2027.

St. Jude Medical Inc's Third-Quarter Profits Held Back by Missed Heart Valve Sale to Iran and Other Factors

Medical device maker St. Jude Medical Inc reported lower third-quarter profits on Wednesday due to a combination of factors, including the loss of an expected sale of heart valves to Iran. The company said profits fell by 12% to $329 million, or $1.06 per share, down from $373 million, or $1.21 per share, in the same period last year. 

Revenue also declined by 3% to $1.33 billion from $1.37 billion a year ago. St. Jude Medical attributed the weaker results to unfavorable foreign exchange rates, a one-time charge related to job cuts, and lower sales of heart valves. The company had expected to sell $25 million worth of heart valves to Iran during the quarter but had to cancel the sale due to ongoing geopolitical tensions and reimposed U.S. sanctions.

Excluding one-time items, St. Jude Medical's profits fell short of analysts' expectations of $1.09 per share.

But analysts are urging caution, pointing to the high failure rate of drug development and the potential for cancer treatments to have severe side effects. 
Ontario-based Parry Medical unveiled results from a Phase III study of its drug nusinersen, which helps to control the amount of RNA in the spinal fluid of people with spinal muscular atrophy, or SMA. The results showed a 37% improvement in walking ability among patients compared to a control group, earning the company $86 million in additional milestone payments. 
Analysts are taking the results in that direction.

I stumbled back, everything I thought I knew

One of the primary reasons why organizational structure is important for effective budgetary control is its influence on communication and decision-making processes. A well-designed organizational structure clarifies the reporting lines and establishes clear responsibilities and authorities. This enables efficient coordination and collaboration, ensuring all departments and individuals are aware of and adhere to the budgetary restrictions. For instance, a hierarchical structure may facilitate top-down communication to ensure that the budgetary control measures are uniform across the organization.
Budget planning is another critical component of achieving effective budgetary control. It involves setting goals, determining resource requirements, and developing strategies to achieve those goals. A well-constructed budget allows businesses to allocate resources strategically, identify potential areas of overspending, and take corrective actions in a timely manner. Moreover, budget planning helps organizations prioritize their investments and minimize wasteful expenses. Without proper budget planning, businesses risk overspending or allocating resources ineffectively, leading to budgetary deviations and financial instability.

Henrik Ibsen's 1879 play'A Doll's House' exemplifies many of the characteristics of the naturalist drama movement of the late 19th century. Naturalism in drama aimed to represent'real life' on stage as truthfully and objectively as possible. Ibsen adopted this approach in'A Doll's House' through focusing on the lives of middle-class people and their daily struggles and relationships. The play has a strong focus on the psychology and inner experiences of the characters in place of melodramatic plotlines and action. The characters are ordinary people grappling with family dynamics, relationships, gender roles and self-identity. This focus on internal, psychological elements was a hallmark of naturalism in drama. 

Ibsen also employed highly detailed, elaborate stage directions in the text of'A Doll's House' in order to prescribe the most realistic and lifelike staging of the play. The stage directions span several pages at the beginning of the play, describing in extensive detail the set, furnishings, lighting and daily activities of the characters.

Hyperlipidemia refers to abnormally high levels of lipids, such as cholesterol and triglycerides, in the blood. Elevated lipid levels are a risk factor for coronary heart disease, including heart attacks and coronary artery disease. There are several classes of pharmaceutical treatments available for hyperlipidemia to help lower lipid levels and reduce coronary heart disease risk.

Statins are the most commonly prescribed class of drugs for lowering cholesterol. Statins work by inhibiting the enzyme HMG-CoA reductase, which plays a key role in cholesterol production. By blocking this enzyme, statins reduce the amount of cholesterol made by the liver. Statins have been shown in numerous large clinical trials to effectively lower LDL or "bad" cholesterol and reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes. Some of the most widely used statins include atorvastatin (Lipitor), simvastatin (Zocor), rosuvastatin (Crestor), and pravastatin (Pravachol). Lowering LDL cholesterol by just 1% can reduce the risk of coronary heart disease by 1 to 2%.

Distinguishing between voiced and voiceless phonemes in English can be challenging for several reasons. Voiced and voiceless pairs of obstruents, like /b/ and /p/, differ primarily in the vibration of the vocal folds during articulation, but this distinction can be subtle and difficult to perceive. This has led some linguists to propose alternative classification systems that aim to capture more salient acoustic properties.

One difficulty in distinguishing voiced and voiceless obstruents is that the primary acoustic cue, vocal fold vibration, is not always clearly perceived. In casual or fast speech, voicing contrasts can be neutralized or obscured. The voicing distinction is also more difficult to perceive for obstruents in word-final position, where vocal fold vibration ends abruptly. These factors can make it challenging for listeners to reliably determine whether an obstruent is voiced or voiceless based only on the presence or absence of vocal fold vibration.

Western Australia’s largest global partnerships in its liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry —Woodside Petroleum and industry giants BHP, Chevron, Shell, and Mitsubishi—announced a plan to double production in the North West Shelf (NWS) project today. The partners have proposed a A$6 billion joint investment to ensure the NWS will continue to operate for decades to come. 

The NWS is one of Australia's crucial LNG production complexes, responsible for about 42% of the country's LNG production. The project, based in Western Australia's Pilbara region, includes five offshore gas and condensate fields and an onshore LNG processing facility near Karratha.

Under the proposed expansion, the project would produce another 6 million tonnes per year. Once completed, the NWS expansion would represent a significant boost to Australia’s natural gas sector, creating jobs and strengthening the economy.

The partners expect to complete the final investment decision (FID) process for the expansion project in the second half of 2021 and begin operations in 2027.

BT Beats Analyst Forecasts With Strong Profits and Growth Despite Competition  

BT, the British telecommunications giant, reported strong profits and revenue growth for the third quarter, beating analyst expectations. The company benefited from increasing broadband subscriptions and mobile users despite facing significant competition in the market.

BT posted a 6% rise in revenue to £5.97 billion for the three months ending December 31, 2019. Pre-tax profits climbed 2% to £2 billion. On an earnings per share basis, BT earned 23.2 pence, ahead of the 21.8 pence forecast by analysts. 

The company added 82,000 new broadband customers, the highest number in more than three years. BT now has over 14 million broadband subscribers, with 60% of those on faster fiber connections. Revenue from consumer broadband services grew 10% from a year earlier.

BT's mobile division, EE, gained 161,000 postpaid mobile subscribers, the most in a quarter since BT acquired EE in 2016. EE now has nearly 32 million total mobile customers. Revenue from mobile services increased 4% from a year ago.

The Building Societies Association (BSA) is considering taking the issue of draft legislation on takeover protection to a European Court of Justice. BSA believes the legislation poses the risk of putting thousands of small British firms and their shareholders, into great financial distress. The proposed legislation, introduced by a coalition government under the Financial Services Bill, enables UK companies to delay the payment of taxes if they have to pay large sums of money to acquire a controlling stake in a business.

The BSA has warned that the legislation could result in thousands of companies having to hand over substantial amounts of cash to acquire a controlling stake in their businesses, leading to difficult financial circumstances and even insolvency. The BSA has suggested that the legislation breaches European Union (EU) merger regulations, creating major legal uncertainties and increasing political risk for the UK.

Additionally, the BSA argues that the UK could fall foul of legal regulations, including those governing cross-border acquisitions, if the legislation is allowed to stand.

So I stumble out when it was closin' time, musta been'round 4 o'clock in the morning, and made my way through some alleys to find the quaint little AirBnB place I'd rented for the week.

Thanks for reading my story!
He’d be thirty-three years old this July. If you could see him now, he’d be laughing.
He’d have a career. A family. A house.
He’d have a girlfriend. Or maybe a wife.
He’d be proud. Happy. Loving.
He would be happy.
Because he had seen the future.
It looked good, he said. Better than good. The best.
He had a plan. He had things he was going to do, places he was going to go.
But the future would never come for him.
He was an angel now. An angel without wings.
He had told the story. And then he’d gone.
She would be twenty-three next month, and while she had a career, a family, and a house, a girlfriend and a potential wife, she was not happy.
He had died when she was six.
A young girl.

A well-designed organizational structure clarifies the reporting lines and establishes clear responsibilities and authorities. This enables efficient coordination and collaboration, ensuring all departments and individuals are aware of and adhere to the budgetary restrictions. For instance, a hierarchical structure may facilitate top-down communication to ensure that the budgetary control measures are uniform across the organization.
Budget planning is another critical component of achieving effective budgetary control. It involves setting goals, determining resource requirements, and developing strategies to achieve those goals. Moreover, budget planning helps organizations prioritize their investments and minimize wasteful expenses. Without proper budget planning, businesses risk overspending or allocating resources ineffectively, leading to budgetary deviations and financial instability.

Henrik Ibsen's 1879 play'A Doll's House' exemplifies many of the characteristics of the naturalist drama movement of the late 19th century. Naturalism in drama aimed to represent'real life' on stage as truthfully and objectively as possible. Ibsen adopted this approach in'A Doll's House' through focusing on the lives of middle-class people and their daily struggles and relationships. The play has a strong focus on the psychology and inner experiences of the characters in place of melodramatic plotlines and action. The characters are ordinary people grappling with family dynamics, relationships, gender roles and self-identity. This focus on internal, psychological elements was a hallmark of naturalism in drama. 

Ibsen also employed highly detailed, elaborate stage directions in the text of'A Doll's House' in order to prescribe the most realistic and lifelike staging of the play. The stage directions span several pages at the beginning of the play, describing in extensive detail the set, furnishings, lighting and daily activities of the characters.

Western Australia’s largest global partnerships in its liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry —Woodside Petroleum and industry giants BHP, Chevron, Shell, and Mitsubishi—announced a plan to double production in the North West Shelf (NWS) project today. The partners have proposed a A$6 billion joint investment to ensure the NWS will continue to operate for decades to come. 

The NWS is one of Australia's crucial LNG production complexes, responsible for about 42% of the country's LNG production. The project, based in Western Australia's Pilbara region, includes five offshore gas and condensate fields and an onshore LNG processing facility near Karratha.

Under the proposed expansion, the project would produce another 6 million tonnes per year. Once completed, the NWS expansion would represent a significant boost to Australia’s natural gas sector, creating jobs and strengthening the economy.

The partners expect to complete the final investment decision (FID) process for the expansion project in the second half of 2021 and begin operations in 2027.

St. Jude Medical attributed the weaker results to unfavorable foreign exchange rates, a one-time charge related to job cuts, and lower sales of heart valves. The company had expected to sell $25 million worth of heart valves to Iran during the quarter but had to cancel the sale due to ongoing geopolitical tensions and reimposed U.S. sanctions.

Excluding one-time items, St. Jude Medical's profits fell short of analysts' expectations of $1.09 per share.

modified: Dreams are funny things. You may think you are just going to sleep, but before you know it you are running through a jungle, struggling to breathe while a panting gorilla looks on.  Then you wake up. I think we all have experienced a dream like this, but what does it mean?  Some believe that it is the way to communicate with the spirit world. Others think it is just a bunch of fluff to help you sleep. I personally think that it is just your imagination at work, like a puzzle.  I have had dreams where I have had two sets of hands.  One set would push me down while the other would play piano.  One time my arms were full of baseballs and my hands had fake fingers that shot holes in the baseballs.  Another time I had my hands bound behind my back and it took two sets of hands to free me.

"Thank you for your time," he quietly said, without any real explanation.

"Oh, don't mention it," I replied, wondering what could have been in the experiment he wanted to end.

The old logging trail was overgrown but still visible to John as he made his way through the dense forest. His backpack was heavy with supplies for his final days. After 60 years of struggling with depression, he was ready to end it. 

As he reached a small clearing, he was surprised to see another man sitting on a large rock, staring intently at a bottle of pills in his hands. John coughed to announce his presence. The man looked up, startled.

They stared at each other for a moment, an unspoken understanding passing between them. "I guess we had the same idea," the man said grimly.

John nodded. "I'm John."

"Mark," the other man replied.  

An awkward silence fell. John didn't know what to say. He had planned to find solitude, not company. But something about knowing this stranger, Mark, made his own decision feel suddenly less sure.

Mark broke the silence.

I thought I was the villain in this tale. I had it all planned out. The traps were set, the evil plot devised, the heroes walking right into my clutches.

Then he did the unthinkable. He didn't fall for any of my tricks or schemes. He evaded every snare.  But he didn't gloat or retaliate. He just gave me that infuriating smile of his, as if he knew something I didn't. 

When I finally had him cornered, monologuing like a fool, he put his hand on my shoulder and said "It doesn't have to be this way." His eyes were unbearably kind.

In that moment, something inside me cracked. The anger and hatred drained away, leaving me hollow. I suddenly saw with awful clarity the depths I had sunk to, the hurt I had caused.

I stumbled back, everything I thought I knew in tatters around me. "What have I done?" I choked out.

It is a bizarre sight, but one that I have embraced with wonder. What used to be a fearful experience has now turned into a cherished routine.

Henrik Ibsen's 1879 play'A Doll's House' exemplifies many of the characteristics of the naturalist drama movement of the late 19th century. Naturalism in drama aimed to represent'real life' on stage as truthfully and objectively as possible. Ibsen adopted this approach in'A Doll's House' through focusing on the lives of middle-class people and their daily struggles and relationships. The play has a strong focus on the psychology and inner experiences of the characters in place of melodramatic plotlines and action. The characters are ordinary people grappling with family dynamics, relationships, gender roles and self-identity. This focus on internal, psychological elements was a hallmark of naturalism in drama. 

Ibsen also employed highly detailed, elaborate stage directions in the text of'A Doll's House' in order to prescribe the most realistic and lifelike staging of the play. The stage directions span several pages at the beginning of the play, describing in extensive detail the set, furnishings, lighting and daily activities of the characters.

Hyperlipidemia refers to abnormally high levels of lipids, such as cholesterol and triglycerides, in the blood. Elevated lipid levels are a risk factor for coronary heart disease, including heart attacks and coronary artery disease. There are several classes of pharmaceutical treatments available for hyperlipidemia to help lower lipid levels and reduce coronary heart disease risk.

Statins are the most commonly prescribed class of drugs for lowering cholesterol. Statins work by inhibiting the enzyme HMG-CoA reductase, which plays a key role in cholesterol production. By blocking this enzyme, statins reduce the amount of cholesterol made by the liver. Statins have been shown in numerous large clinical trials to effectively lower LDL or "bad" cholesterol and reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes. Some of the most widely used statins include atorvastatin (Lipitor), simvastatin (Zocor), rosuvastatin (Crestor), and pravastatin (Pravachol).

This has led some linguists to propose alternative classification systems that aim to capture more salient acoustic properties.

One difficulty in distinguishing voiced and voiceless obstruents is that the primary acoustic cue, vocal fold vibration, is not always clearly perceived. On Thursday, U.S. envoy to East Asia, Daniel Kritenbrink told reporters at a briefing, "For the United States, Hong Kong's autonomy, its freedoms, and the quality of life of its residents are of great importance and will remain so."
He went on to reaffirm Washington's support for the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration, which laid out the terms of the handover of Hong Kong from Britain to China in 1997. The agreement was designed to guarantee rights and freedoms to Hong Kong's citizens, including the right to vote, free speech, and an independent judiciary under the principle of "one country, two systems."
However, many Hong Kong citizens and international observers have grown increasingly concerned that China is steadily chipping away at Hong Kong's autonomy and freedoms.

The U.S. Department of Justice today asked the Supreme Court to lift a temporary suspension of new federal regulations aimed at opening local telephone markets to increased competition. In a filing with the high court, the Justice Department argued that a recent appeals court ruling blocking the new rules could undermine efforts to spur innovation and lower prices in the telecommunications industry.

The Federal Communications Commission last year approved new rules that make it easier for companies to enter local phone markets dominated by major carriers like AT&T Inc. and Verizon Communications Inc. The rules curb regulatory requirements on new entrants and cap the access fees they pay to connect calls. A coalition of telecom trade groups challenged the rules in court, arguing the FCC overstepped its authority.

BT Beats Analyst Forecasts With Strong Profits and Growth Despite Competition  

BT, the British telecommunications giant, reported strong profits and revenue growth for the third quarter, beating analyst expectations. The company benefited from increasing broadband subscriptions and mobile users despite facing significant competition in the market.

BT posted a 6% rise in revenue to £5.97 billion for the three months ending December 31, 2019. Pre-tax profits climbed 2% to £2 billion. On an earnings per share basis, BT earned 23.2 pence, ahead of the 21.8 pence forecast by analysts. 

The company added 82,000 new broadband customers, the highest number in more than three years. BT now has over 14 million broadband subscribers, with 60% of those on faster fiber connections. Revenue from consumer broadband services grew 10% from a year earlier.

BT's mobile division, EE, gained 161,000 postpaid mobile subscribers, the most in a quarter since BT acquired EE in 2016. EE now has nearly 32 million total mobile customers. Revenue from mobile services increased 4% from a year ago.

The little Jesus rolled his eyes. “Grandma?” he asked.
“No, son. Grandma had the same fairy dust idea when she was your age.”

“So it was my imagination,” said the little Jesus. “I am the same age as Jesus.

The old logging trail was overgrown but still visible to John as he made his way through the dense forest. His backpack was heavy with supplies for his final days. After 60 years of struggling with depression, he was ready to end it. 

As he reached a small clearing, he was surprised to see another man sitting on a large rock, staring intently at a bottle of pills in his hands. John coughed to announce his presence. The man looked up, startled.

They stared at each other for a moment, an unspoken understanding passing between them. "I guess we had the same idea," the man said grimly.

John nodded. "I'm John."

"Mark," the other man replied.  

An awkward silence fell. John didn't know what to say. He had planned to find solitude, not company. But something about knowing this stranger, Mark, made his own decision feel suddenly less sure.

Mark broke the silence.

Then he did the unthinkable. He didn't fall for any of my tricks or schemes. He evaded every snare.  But he didn't gloat or retaliate. He just gave me that infuriating smile of his, as if he knew something I didn't.

Every day, like clockwork, my normal day consists of 25 hours instead of 24. It's something I have grown accustomed to, as though I am given an extra slice of time to spend just the way I please. Once a day, for an hour, the world stops except for me.
In this enchanted hour, I am free to explore the stillness that surrounds me. The silence is profound and soothing, as if the universe wants to give me undivided attention. Every day, I use this extraordinary hour to immerse myself in the beauty of the world that temporarily rests.
As soon as the clock strikes the designated moment, everything freezes in place. People halt mid-step, birds suspended in the air, and leaves hold their breath on the branches. It is a bizarre sight, but one that I have embraced with wonder. What used to be a fearful experience has now turned into a cherished routine.

As I walked around, admiring the architecture and the hustle and bustle of the busy streets, I couldn't help but feel inspired. I started typing on my phone, weaving my experiences and surroundings into a story.

At a café, I took a break and looked up from my phone screen. The aroma of fresh coffee filled the air as baristas expertly brewed different blends. I added the café setting to my story, describing the espresso machine's steam and the sound of beans being ground.

Feeling adventurous, I headed towards the river and walked across a bridge. Below, boats floated lazily downstream.
